translation: Target is the proposition that for every set K of arithmetic sentences and every arithmetic theory (set of arithmetic sentences) F, if: (1) F is recursively enumerable, (2) every theorem of 𝗜𝚺₁ is a theorem of F, (3) F is consistent (does not prove a contradiction), (4) the set of all theorems of F is a subset of K, and (5) K contains the local reflection schema for F.craig—that is, for every arithmetic sentence σ, the sentence Prov_{F.craig}(⌜σ⌝) 🡒 σ belongs to K, where F.craig is the Δ₁-presented axiom set with the same theorems as F obtained from F by Craig's trick—then the set of all theorems of F is a strict (proper) subset of K (i.e., F.theory ⊆ K and K is not a subset of F.theory). Nothing further is required of K (it need not be deductively closed, consistent, true in the standard model, or recursively enumerable), and F need not be deductively closed, Δ₁-presented, or true in the standard model.

divergences.description: TARGET adds F.theory ⊆ K as an explicit hypothesis in the antecedent, thereby assuming the inclusion half of the claimed conclusion F.theory ⊂ K (which is F.theory ⊆ K ∧ ¬(K ⊆ F.theory)) rather than deriving F ⊆ K from K knowing F is sound as in Koellner's conditional. Because K is also left completely unconstrained (no deductive closure, arithmetic strength, or epistemic axioms), K plays no substantive mathematical role: TARGET is purely set-theoretically equivalent to ¬(F.craig.localReflectionOn Set.univ ⊆ F.theory), so it only establishes K ⊈ F.theory rather than deriving F ⊊ K from the reflection scheme.

TARGET adds Def4 F (Entailment.Consistent F) as an explicit hypothesis while omitting any soundness or factivity assumption on K (such as Def3 K). In Koellner's source, the conditional applies to any formal system F without presupposing F's consistency, since K's factivity makes the antecedent false when F is inconsistent; however, because Def3 K and Def9 K F together entail Def4 F, trading factivity of K for consistency of F yields a stronger statement whenever K is sound, though it allows unsound or inconsistent K and restricts F to consistent theories.

TARGET restricts F via [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F], whereas Koellner's conditional quantifies over any formal system F (and Penrose over any algorithm), with arithmetic strength belonging to EA/K rather than to F. Weak formal systems not extending 𝗜𝚺₁ are excluded by TARGET.

Def9 K F fixes the specific Δ₁-presentation F.craig obtained by Craig's trick rather than quantifying over arbitrary Δ₁-presentations or formulas F(x) representing F; because provability and local reflection are intensional, this restricts the antecedent to one canonical presentation.

As explicitly declared by the author, TARGET states a meta-level proposition over arbitrary sets K of first-order arithmetic sentences rather than a theorem inside Epistemic Arithmetic (EA or EA_T) with an object-language knowledge operator K.

judgement.summary: TARGET diverges materially from Koellner's conditional 'if K knows F is sound then F ⊊ K' because it explicitly assumes F.theory ⊆ K as a premise while leaving K completely unconstrained, reducing the formalization to a set-theoretic wrapper around the fact that no consistent r.e. extension of 𝗜𝚺₁ proves its own local reflection schema. It also adds external hypotheses on F (consistency and 𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F) and fixes the Craig's-trick presentation F.craig rather than deriving those conditions from epistemic properties of K.
